findings.title: Google Calendar stores the zod SafeParse wrapper object as the credential key
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns the raw `safeParse` result (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed data. Previously this line was `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` which returned the token object directly. Now `key` is the wrapper object and it is written to `credential.key` on line 98-101. The next time this credential is loaded, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) will fail because `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `expiry_date` etc. are nested under `data`. This corrupts every Google Calendar credential on its first token refresh and happens regardless of whether credential sharing is enabled. Use `.data` from the return value (or have the helper return the parsed data).

findings.title: `prisma` is used but never imported in Salesforce CalendarService
findings.body: The new `getClient` code calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` on line 96, but there is no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` in this file (imports are lines 1-20). This is a type-check failure and, at runtime, a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` thrown from `getClient`, which runs in the constructor via `this.conn = this.getClient(credential)`. Every Salesforce booking operation will fail. Add the missing import.

findings.title: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses `z.string().toString()` as keys, which evaluates to "[object Object]" and strips every field except access_token
findings.body: Computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal string `"[object Object]"` (ZodType does not override `toString`), so the second overwrites the first and the schema is effectively `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() })`. The intended 'any numeric property is the expiry' / 'allow other properties' behaviour does not exist. Because `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, in sharing mode `refreshTokenResponse.data` is `{ access_token }` only: expiry fields are discarded (so Office365's `expires_in` and Zoom's `expires_in` are undefined → `isExpired` stays true and tokens are refreshed on every single API call; Zoom computes `expiry_date = NaN` on line 122 of its adapter and the stored key then fails `zoomTokenSchema.parse` on the next load). A permissive schema needs `.passthrough()`/`z.record` or explicit optional fields; this one needs a unit test.

findings.title: Placeholder `refresh_token: "refresh_token"` overwrites real refresh tokens when spread into stored credentials
findings.body: When the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the helper mutates `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. In `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` line 264 the data is spread over the existing credentials (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`), so whenever Microsoft (or the self-hoster's sync endpoint, which per the comments 'should only contain the access token and expiry date') omits a refresh token, the user's real refresh token in the database is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token". Previously, with `refresh_token` optional and absent, the spread left the stored value intact. After this, any later refresh against Microsoft fails permanently and the user must reconnect. The helper should not inject a fake refresh token; callers should preserve the existing one when none is returned.

findings.title: Sync-endpoint branch returns a raw fetch `Response`, but Google/HubSpot/Zoho callers expect SDK-specific shapes
findings.body: When `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set the helper returns the `fetch` `Response` object, whereas the fallback returns whatever `refreshFunction` returns. Callers are written against the fallback shape: Google Calendar does `res?.data.access_token` (googleapis `GaxiosResponse`) → `data` is undefined → TypeError, swallowed by the catch and the expired token is kept; HubSpot treats the return as a `HubspotToken` → `expiresIn`/`accessToken` undefined, `setAccessToken(undefined)`, and the `Response` object (with `expiryDate: NaN`) is written to `credential.key`, corrupting the credential; Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `tokenInfo.data.error` (axios shape) → TypeError. So four of the nine integrations this PR wires up do not work in sharing mode. The helper should normalise the sync response (e.g. `await response.json()`) and each caller must handle that shape explicitly.

findings.title: `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by app directory name, not slug, so lookups fail for most apps
findings.body: `appStoreMetadata` (from `apps.metadata.generated.ts`) is keyed by the app's directory name (`googlecalendar`, `zoomvideo`, `office365calendar`, `office365video`, `larkcalendar`, ...), not by its slug (`google-calendar`, `zoom`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `lark-calendar`). Indexing it with `app.slug` therefore returns `undefined` for exactly the apps this PR targets, and the webhook responds 404 "App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug" even though the slug is correct. Only apps whose dirName equals their slug (hubspot, salesforce, zohocrm, zoho-bigin) would work. Use `getAppFromSlug()` from `@calcom/app-store/utils`, or select `dirName` from the `App` row and index with that.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId` where `refreshOAuthTokens` expects the user id
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFn, appSlug, userId)` sends `calcomUserId: userId` to the self-hoster's sync endpoint and uses `userId` being non-null to decide whether the credential belongs to a user. Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId` as that third argument (every other integration passes `credential.userId`). Consequences: the sync endpoint is asked for tokens for the wrong user (a credential id that happens to match some other user's id), and team credentials (userId null) are also routed to the sync endpoint because credentialId is always a number. Pass `credential.userId` instead.

findings.title: Zoom sends `appSlug: "zoomvideo"` to the sync endpoint while the app's slug is `"zoom"`
findings.body: Every other integration passes its real slug (`google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `hubspot`, ...) as the `appSlug` argument to `refreshOAuthTokens`, and the inbound `/api/webhook/app-credential` endpoint also identifies apps by slug. Zoom passes its directory name `"zoomvideo"`. A self-hoster keying their endpoint on the slug they used when pushing credentials (`zoom`) will not recognise `zoomvideo`, so Zoom token refresh via the sync endpoint fails. Use `"zoom"`.

findings.title: Request to the credential sync endpoint carries no authentication
findings.body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` only sends `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body, with no shared secret, signature or bearer token. The endpoint must therefore hand out live OAuth access tokens for any user id to any caller that can reach it, since the self-hoster has no way to verify the request originated from Cal.com. A `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` / `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` pair already exists for the inbound direction; the same header should be sent on this outbound request (and `response.ok` should be checked) so the self-hoster can authenticate it.

findings.title: Salesforce now hits the token endpoint on every instantiation, and the refreshed token is not even used
findings.body: `getClient` (called from the constructor for every booking/update/delete) now unconditionally POSTs to `login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and writes the result to the database, regardless of whether the stored token is still valid; previously jsforce refreshed lazily. The new `jsforce.Connection` on line 101-108 is still constructed with the old `credentialKey.access_token`/`instance_url`, so the freshly obtained token is stored but never used by this request. Additionally, this path bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce does not participate in credential sharing at all, and the check `response.statusText !== "OK"` on line 86 is fragile (statusText is not guaranteed; use `response.ok`). The `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` branch on line 92 is dead because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with `!==` (not constant-time)
findings.body: The shared secret from the request header is compared to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` with a plain string inequality, which short-circuits on the first differing byte and leaks timing information about the secret to an attacker who can make repeated requests. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers (as the Stripe/other webhook handlers in the repo do).

findings.title: No method check and unhandled parse/decrypt errors return 500s
findings.body: The handler accepts any HTTP method; a GET has no body so `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(undefined)` throws a ZodError that propagates as an unhandled 500. Likewise `symmetricDecrypt` (line 58) throws on a wrong key length or tampered ciphertext and `JSON.parse` throws on non-JSON plaintext, all surfacing as 500 with a stack trace instead of a 400. Reject non-POST with 405, use `safeParse`, and wrap decryption in a try/catch returning 400.

findings.title: Updating an existing credential does not clear the `invalid` flag
findings.body: When the self-hoster pushes fresh keys for a credential that Cal.com previously marked `invalid: true` (e.g. after an `invalid_grant` from Google or Zoom), the update only sets `key`. The credential stays flagged invalid, so the UI keeps showing it as broken and some code paths skip it, even though the synced keys are now good. The update should also set `invalid: false`.

findings.title: No tests for the new shared token-parsing/refresh helpers or the webhook endpoint
findings.body: The PR introduces a shared parser that is now in the refresh path of Google Calendar, Office 365, Zoom and Salesforce, plus a new credential-ingest webhook, with no unit or integration tests (the description acknowledges this). Trivial tests would have caught that the 'minimum' schema strips every field but `access_token`, that the helper returns the SafeParse wrapper rather than the data (corrupting Google credentials), and that the webhook's `appStoreMetadata[slug]` lookup returns undefined for `google-calendar`. Please add tests for `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (both modes), `refreshOAuthTokens` return shape, and the webhook's happy/unhappy paths before merging.
